qualifying_findings.title: OpenAI-hosted collective cyber-defense letter warns of AI-enabled cyberattack acceleration

visible_dates.date_type: visible via secondary publication; primary page did not expose a machine-readable timestamp in fetched content

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: More than 100 organizations, including frontier AI companies, cloud providers, security vendors, and critical-infrastructure stakeholders, called for urgent cyber-defense action against increasingly widespread and sophisticated AI-enabled attacks. The primary letter asks organizations to fix high-risk weaknesses, deploy least privilege and strong access controls, continuously test defenses against frontier cyber capabilities, share threat intelligence, and make defender access to capable AI available during major incidents.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: primary official open letter corroborated by reputable secondary reporting
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AI-enabled cyber defense and critical-infrastructure security operations; no product version boundary
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a governance and risk-management signal that frames cyber-capable AI as an active threat multiplier and names concrete controls: least privilege, access controls, defense-in-depth, continuous testing, observability, traceable agent identities, trusted access programs, and incident-response access to defensive models.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad company and ecosystem-signatory context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General AI-generated-code quality and development workflow implications belong upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain the AI-enabled attack acceleration, defensive-control, incident-response, and agent identity implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on publication date from Axios and primary-source content from OpenAI; primary OpenAI page did not expose an explicit visible date in fetched text.

qualifying_findings.title: SiYuan MCP asset.upload path traversal enables prompt-induced local file exposure
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: SiYuan before v3.8.1 accepted arbitrary absolute file paths in the MCP asset.upload tool without workspace boundary validation. A prompt-injection path can induce an AI Agent to upload sensitive host files such as SSH keys or cloud credentials into the workspace after a category-level approval that does not show the exact file path.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication plus GitHub security advisory with technical details
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: SiYuan <= 3.8.0; patched in v3.8.1 according to NVD/GitHub metadata
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: It demonstrates that human approval is insufficient when the approval hides tool arguments; AI tool file access needs explicit workspace and sensitive-path enforcement.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: SiYuan product/background belongs upstream if durable product coverage is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP approval UX and tool-governance pattern belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain the MCP file-boundary bypass, prompt-injection trigger, and sensitive-file exposure.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence. GitHub advisory has older publication date, but NVD publication is inside the cutoff window.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-use inspector proxy SSRF accepts caller-supplied internal targets
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: The mcp-use inspector proxy forwarded requests to a destination supplied through the X-Target-URL header or __mcp_target parameter without rejecting loopback, link-local, private addresses, names resolving to those ranges, or unsafe redirect targets. Current code adds isSafeProxyTarget checks and redirect bounds.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication with public repository advisory references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mcp-use versions <= 2.3.2; fixed code validates resolved addresses before proxying
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP inspection and debugging surfaces can become internal-network read channels unless proxy destinations are constrained before and after redirects.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP debugging workflow belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain SSRF, redirect validation, and inspector trust-boundary implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from structured NVD result; GitHub page was accessible as a referenced advisory but publication date in fetched browser content may be older than NVD.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-go HTTP transports missed Host validation, enabling DNS rebinding
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: mcp-go HTTP transports accepted requests over loopback without validating the Host header, so a browser-based DNS rebinding path could reach Streamable HTTP or SSE MCP endpoints. The referenced fix is v0.56.0.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication with project pull request and release references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local MCP transports need browser-origin and Host-header protections because browser content can bridge into loopback services used by agents.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: mcp-go SDK entity coverage belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP transport deployment practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain local transport Host validation and browser-to-agent attack path.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD dates and project fix references.

qualifying_findings.title: ToolUniverse unauthenticated Python executor sandbox escape permits RCE
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: ToolUniverse ran caller-supplied Python inside a sandbox that could be escaped while the server required no authentication. The python_code_executor tool used denied-list source inspection that could be bypassed to reach arbitrary code execution.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication with GitHub advisory and maintainer pull request references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent tool ecosystems frequently expose code-execution tools; unauthenticated or deny-list-only sandboxes collapse the boundary between AI tool invocation and host execution.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent tool execution workflow belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain unauthenticated tool execution, sandbox escape, and RCE risk.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD structured record; fixed-version detail should be rechecked during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: UI-TARS desktop MCP transports bind broadly without authentication
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: UI-TARS-desktop started Streamable HTTP and SSE MCP transports on all interfaces when no host was supplied, while authentication middleware did not require caller credentials. The exposed transport could provide arbitrary command execution through agent infrastructure.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication with public commit and pull request references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: UI-TARS-desktop agent-infra MCP HTTP server at commit e9f3387-era source; fix referenced in c2ad42e3 and PR 1918
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Desktop agent infrastructure with action tools must default to loopback-only, authenticated transports; otherwise local automation becomes a remotely reachable execution service.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: UI-TARS desktop product/entity context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain unauthenticated MCP transport and command-execution exposure.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD publication and project references.

qualifying_findings.title: Bifrost AI Gateway multimodal fetch guard misses internal address ranges
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Bifrost's isPublicIP guard in FetchAndEncodeURL allowed CGNAT, IPv6 6to4, NAT64, and deprecated site-local addresses. A client controlling multimodal image or document URLs in Bedrock or Vertex request paths could trigger SSRF from the gateway to internal services, including cloud metadata endpoint embeddings.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication plus GitHub security advisory with technical detail
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Bifrost prior to core v1.5.17; GitHub advisory lists <= 1.5.15 and patched >= 1.5.16, while NVD references v1.5.17 release
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI gateways that fetch multimodal inputs are network trust boundaries; IP classification must cover cloud, IPv6 transition, private, and metadata address cases.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General multimodal gateway integration practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain AI gateway SSRF and cloud-metadata exposure boundary.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on vulnerability mechanics; fixed-version boundary should be reconciled during ingest because GitHub advisory and NVD references differ slightly.

qualifying_findings.title: Portkey AI Gateway proxy route lacks request validation and permits SSRF
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Portkey AI Gateway through 1.15.2 has an SSRF flaw in /v1/proxy/* because the route lacks requestValidator middleware. Attackers can set x-portkey-custom-host to internal addresses.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication with public repository and issue references
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Model gateway proxy routes must validate destination authority because gateway credentials and network position can expose internal infrastructure.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Portkey AI Gateway product context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General gateway deployment practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain route-level SSRF and request-validation implication.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from NVD publication; maintainer patch status should be rechecked during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: FastGPT WeChat outLink endpoints allow unauthenticated cross-tenant bot hijack
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: FastGPT before v4.15.2 allowed WeChat iLink share-channel endpoints to mutate outLink bot credentials based only on public shareId values. An unauthenticated attacker could wipe a victim team's bot token or bind the victim outLink to the attacker's WeChat bot.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication plus GitHub security advisory
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: FastGPT prior to v4.15.2; advisory describes main at commit 4066f3c1
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI application channel integrations need tenant-scoped authorization; public share identifiers must not authorize bot credential writes or channel binding.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General AI app channel integration practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain tenant authorization, bot-token integrity, and public-shareId risk.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence; GitHub advisory date predates cutoff but NVD publication qualifies.

qualifying_findings.title: Stable Diffusion WebUI exposes cleartext auth flags through cmd-flags endpoint

visible_dates.date_type: GitHub Advisory Database published and updated
NVD published via GitHub advisory page

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Stable Diffusion WebUI through 1.10.1 exposes parsed command-line arguments at /sdapi/v1/cmd-flags, including gradio_auth and api_auth values in cleartext. Unauthenticated attackers can retrieve credentials and use them to access the application.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database and NVD in-window publication
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Stable Diffusion WebUI through 1.10.1; patched version unknown in GitHub advisory
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Local or hosted model UIs often become shared AI workbenches; exposing auth flags turns configuration introspection into credential theft and unauthorized model/application access.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General local AI workbench operation belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain credential disclosure and exposed AI UI configuration boundary.

qualifying_findings.title: VoltAgent memory APIs miss conversation ownership checks

visible_dates.date_type: NVD published via GitHub advisory page

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: VoltAgent through 2.1.20 fails to validate conversation ownership in memory API handlers. Authenticated users can read, modify, or delete other users' conversations and messages by supplying caller-controlled identifiers.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database and NVD in-window publication
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: VoltAgent through 2.1.20; patched version unknown in GitHub advisory
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent memory stores are sensitive identity and context boundaries; missing object ownership checks expose cross-user conversation data and allow memory tampering.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General agent memory architecture practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain cross-user memory authorization and tampering risk.

qualifying_findings.title: Gitingest host-prefix validation can disclose GitHub tokens to attacker hosts

visible_dates.date_type: GitHub Advisory Database published and updated
NVD published via GitHub advisory page

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Gitingest through 0.3.1 accepts any hostname with a git., gitlab., or github. prefix instead of enforcing known-host membership. Attackers can submit crafted URLs that trigger outbound connections to attacker-controlled hosts and disclose GitHub personal access tokens through HTTP basic credentials.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database and NVD in-window publication
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Gitingest through 0.3.1; patched version unknown in GitHub advisory
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Repository-to-context ingestion tools must pin trusted hosts before attaching credentials; otherwise AI context builders become credential exfiltration paths.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General code ingestion and context-building workflow belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain credential forwarding, host validation, and AI context supply-chain implications.

qualifying_findings.title: Bisheng workflow callback endpoint permits unauthenticated SSRF

visible_dates.date_type: GitHub Advisory Database published and updated
NVD published via GitHub advisory page

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Bisheng through 2.6.0-fix2 has an unauthenticated SSRF in POST /api/v1/workflow/report/callback. The endpoint lacks authentication, URL scheme restrictions, and host filtering; captured responses can be retrieved from object storage using caller-supplied object names.

qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Bisheng through 2.6.0-fix2; patched version unknown in GitHub advisory
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Workflow/report callbacks in AI application platforms need authentication and egress controls because they may bridge attacker input to internal services and stored response artifacts.

upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain unauthenticated callback SSRF and object-storage response exposure.

qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published three ServiceNow AI platform records: a code-injection vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated arbitrary code execution in certain circumstances, an improper access-control vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated creation or modification of records, and a SQL-injection vulnerability that could allow unauthenticated SQL execution. ServiceNow lists the issues as remediated.

qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ServiceNow AI platform; exact affected product versions not fully visible from unauthenticated fetched sources
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Enterprise AI platforms often hold workflow, knowledge, and automation authority; unauthenticated code execution, record modification, and SQL execution affect the platform trust boundary.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General enterprise workflow adoption context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain AI platform code/data access boundary and unauthenticated exploit implications.

qualifying_findings.title: Spring AI advisory cluster affects PDF ingestion, ONNX cache, resource cache, and Redis chat memory
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: NVD published multiple Spring AI records inside the window. CVE-2026-47851 is a PDF document reader StackOverflowError caused by deeply nested or cyclic table-of-contents data. CVE-2026-47852 allows local ONNX model substitution through deterministic cache-path precreation. CVE-2026-59294 is arbitrary file write through URI fragment path traversal in ResourceCacheService for model/tokenizer resources. CVE-2026-59319 is RediSearch query injection in RedisChatMemoryRepository.findByMetadata from unescaped metadata values. Spring advisories list fixed versions including 2.0.1, 2.0.0.1, 1.1.9, and 1.0.10 for the fetched Spring pages.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window publication plus vendor advisories with older primary publication dates
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Spring AI 2.0.0, 1.1.0-1.1.8, and 1.0.x ranges vary by CVE; fixed versions include 2.0.1, 2.0.0.1, 1.1.9, and 1.0.10 for fetched advisories
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The cluster spans AI ingestion availability, model artifact substitution, resource-cache file writes, and chat-memory query injection, all recurring AI application trust boundaries.

upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General Spring AI implementation practice belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Retain AI ingestion, model-cache, resource-cache, and memory-store security implications.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence on NVD publication timing. Primary Spring publication dates are outside the window, so this qualifies as in-window NVD publication rather than new vendor disclosure.
